headline: Storm Readiness AI
content_summary: AI-powered storm preparedness & response intelligence. Team of 4, hackathon submission.
notes_context: Opening framing: this is a decision-support system, not a forecast model.

headline: Forecasts say where the storm goes -- not what it costs your county
content_summary: Three user types, one plan: emergency managers (own staging decisions), organizations (resource needs + facilities at risk), residents (plain-language alerts). Key takeaway: most counties/nonprofits lack the 24/7 ops-center capacity large operators have.
notes_context: S2 Problem and users. Quote 'staging decisions are made under forecast uncertainty' and the 24/7 ops center gap.

headline: The pipeline mirrors the sponsor's own seven-stage design, stage for stage
content_summary: Detection to Forecast to Impact Prediction to Risk Assessment to Resource Analysis to Recommended Actions to Human Decision. Key takeaway: every advisory re-runs all seven stages automatically; a human still approves.
source_material: proposal.md S2.1 (demo flow / architecture mirror), S6
notes_context: Explicitly call out this is sponsor's own suggested Big Idea flow, matched stage for stage -- this is a relevance signal for judges.

headline: All 10 MVP-required components ship -- three are the ones teams skip
content_summary: NL interface (chat backed by agent tool-calling), why an area is high-risk (feature importance in plain language), underlying data/sources (provenance panel). Key takeaway: full 10-row compliance table in appendix.
notes_context: Sponsor brief lists 10 required MVP components; none deferred. These 3 are commonly missed by other teams -- emphasize as a scoring differentiator (relevance + usability).

headline: Each job goes to the tool that's actually good at it
content_summary: Hazard scenarios (NHC forecast-error AR(1)) to Impact model (XGBoost, 10yr EAGLE-I) to Staging optimizer (2-stage stochastic, Bhattarai and Song/Clemson) to AI agent (orchestrates, model-agnostic). Key takeaway: the one failure we can't accept is an LLM inventing quantities in a life-safety setting -- this design rules it out.
notes_context: Core technical approach slide. Mention Bhattarai & Song is a published Clemson method, reused for scenario generation and staging, extended with an outage-driven resource layer.

headline: Every AI output is checked against the models before a human ever sees it
content_summary: 4 checks: numbers match models, confidence fits lead time, required steps followed, actionable (LLM-as-judge). Key takeaway: this is the differentiator, not a bolt-on.
notes_context: Trust layer is explicitly the key differentiator per task brief. Emphasize LLM-as-judge is validated against human labels before its scores are trusted.

headline: Runs end-to-end on GCP's serverless tier -- no BigQuery required
content_summary: Left: simplified data flow (sources to models to agent/trust to app). Right: Cloud Storage/DuckDB, Cloud Run, Firestore, Cloud Scheduler, Vertex AI or self-hosted Gemma. Key takeaway: the LLM is a config setting, not an architecture decision.
notes_context: Model-agnostic: Gemini, Claude via Vertex, or open-weights Gemma via vLLM on Cloud Run GPU. No BigQuery needed -- data is small once aggregated.

headline: Every data source is public, grouped into three categories
content_summary: Hazard & forecast (NHC advisories/GIS, forecast-error stats, HURDAT2); impact & vulnerability (EAGLE-I 2014-2024, Census/ACS, CDC SVI, FEMA NRI); assets, guidance & phase-2 (HIFLD/OSM facilities, FEMA distribution centers, Ready.gov guidance; phase-2: NFHL, Overture roads, HIFLD grid). Key takeaway: all public, access confirmed before dependency.
notes_context: Mention EAGLE-I coverage varies by utility/year, normalized by covered customers. Considered-and-not-used sources (S8.1) available if asked.

headline: Backtested leave-one-storm-out against ten years of real outages, never on hindsight
content_summary: 4 questions: impact model MAE/recall vs wind-threshold and NRI-only baselines; staging unmet demand vs single-track and shelter-only baselines; scenario calibration; trust layer mismatch/block/approve rates. Key takeaway: candidate storms Florence (reproduction), Ian, Helene, Milton.
notes_context: Florence is the credibility step (reproduces Bhattarai & Song's own case study) before generalizing to Ian/Helene/Milton. Archived forecasts used as inputs, not best tracks, to avoid hindsight leakage.

headline: Multi-hazard is scoped and data-ready -- deliberately not built for the MVP
content_summary: MVP ships one impact model, backtested on 10 years of real data, not several untested models by Oct 5. Flood/road/transit are the sponsor's own phase-2 examples; data already scoped (NFHL, Overture, HIFLD). Next model after MVP follows same leave-one-storm-out discipline. Key takeaway: deferred by design, not by gap.
notes_context: This directly answers a likely judge question: why only power outages? Answer is discipline, not limitation -- one rigorously tested model beats three untested ones under an 11-day timeline.

headline: Designed to keep running every hurricane season at near-zero idle cost
content_summary: Idle: Cloud Scheduler polls NHC every 6h, services scale to zero. Auto-activates when a storm threatens US land. Public post-storm scorecard published after every storm. Pilot partner sought for 2027 season. Key takeaway: continuously re-tested against real events.
notes_context: Speaks to impact + presentation scoring -- this isn't a one-off hackathon demo, it's built to operate.

headline: Eleven days to build freeze, four workstreams running in parallel
content_summary: Timeline: Sep24-25 proposal/architecture; Sep26-29 pipeline+scenarios+baseline+agent skeleton; Sep30-Oct2 backtest+optimizer+trust layer; Oct3-5 end-to-end replay, build freeze; Oct5-9 demo video, submit. Workstreams A data/impact, B scenarios/optimization, C agent/trust, D app/accessibility/demo. Key takeaway: build freeze Oct 5, submit by Oct 9 9PM PT.
notes_context: 4-person team, 1 workstream owner each (owners TBD per proposal header).

headline: Four sponsor decisions would materially change what we can build
content_summary: Proprietary models + Vertex billing coverage; GPU quota (>=1 NVIDIA L4) for the open-weights path; BigQuery disabled vs. unbudgeted; post-hackathon hosting (whose GCP project). Key takeaway: system is model-agnostic and works either way -- these answers shape scope, not feasibility.
notes_context: Full list has 9 questions (S14); these 4 are the ones the task brief asked to foreground. Scope/data/repo questions (3,6,7,9) available in Q&A if asked.
